mtpd.reason: Stated directly; consistent with the grid, whose worst rating is 3 at every horizon and never reaches the intolerable level 4.

rto.quote: IT event management has an RTO of more than 168 hours, because financial and operational impacts of an outage are to be expected.
rto.speaker: Marek Sobotta
rto.reason: The process owner states an RTO of more than 168 hours over an MTPD past the last horizon, so it is carried as stated.

rpo.reason: Nobody stated an RPO; as a best judgement the monitoring data of IT events can be re-gathered within a day, so <24 h.

dependencies.heard: monitoring of IT events relies on monitoring/alerting tooling
dependencies.quote: The IT event management process covers monitoring and managing IT events, to ensure the continuity of IT services.

conflicts.about: MTPD: the grid (2025) gives no MTPD within horizons by the method's rule, the draft says >168 h

sides.claim: no MTPD within horizons (the method's rule over the grid, 2025)
sides.speaker: method

conflicts.why: The method derives the MTPD from the grid; the other figure is the thing to explain.

gaps.what: The interview names no sub-steps beyond monitoring/managing events and pre-selecting critical events, no resources, no explicit dependency list and no RPO; also the RTO '>168 h' sits exactly at the last horizon.
gaps.ask: Which single activity definition from last cycle's record 3.6 should this BIA carry, what resources does IT event management depend on, and what RPO and recovery target do you confirm?
